depth_findings.text: Concurrent first Space-workspace calls race: ensure_sandbox_lease and ensure_hydrated_workspace (sandbox_lease.rs, about lines 106-130 and 183) check the cache, then create with no per-run guard. cache_sandbox_lease and cache_hydrated_workspace (state.rs, about lines 283 and 307) are unconditional inserts, and release uploads only the cached tree. Two calls in one round can orphan a second lease and directory, and a write that lands there is never uploaded although the tool said it was saved. This blocks switching WORKSPACE_TOOLS to all. Fix: serialise per-run first-call setup (per-run mutex or OnceCell in StateStore).

To verify: a parked Do run keeps its hydrated tree and lease only in process memory. The upload runs only at terminal finalisation (agent.rs about line 1861, release_sandbox_lease_if_any). A run parked after a workspace_edit and resumed on another replica, or after a restart, re-hydrates from the Space base and loses the overlay, though the earlier result said it was saved. Verify with a park-resume test that crosses a fresh StateStore. This blocks all.

The direct ExecuteStep RPC (grpc.rs, about line 1367, then execute_step_inner) applies no plan-mode, leaf or autonomy-rung refusal. Those checks live only in the agent loop (agent.rs about lines 3376, 3423 and 3566). save_memory already has this gap. Background processes started by process_start keep writing into the Space tree after the call returns. The write lock covers only each call's own execution, so a later process write can overwrite an edit and the model is not told.

To verify: workspace_read returns raw file text, including secret-shaped text the run's own code wrote into the tree (uploads are redacted; the local tree is not). I found no output scrub on this path. Check whether the transcript scrub covers tool results.

The process-tool arm holds the exclusive lock for read, list, signal and stdin too. Narrowing it to start and stdin would keep reads concurrent.

state.rs take_hydrated_workspace removes the run's workspace lock entry (state.rs:316). A call that started before keeps its Arc, but a call that starts after gets a new lock and loses exclusion. Confirm no workspace or process call can run after the run's terminal release.

There is no per-run guard on the first workspace setup. ensure_sandbox_lease and ensure_hydrated_workspace check the cache and then create, and the state.rs cache_* calls insert unconditionally. Two first workspace calls in one round can each create a lease and a tree. An edit that lands in the orphaned tree is never uploaded, although the tool reported it as saved. This must be serialised before WORKSPACE_TOOLS=all.

A parked Do run keeps its hydrated overlay only in process memory, and the upload runs only at terminal release. A park and resume on another replica, or after a restart, re-hydrates from the Space base and silently loses a workspace_edit that already reported durability run_overlay. Needs a park-resume test across a fresh StateStore before all.

The direct ExecuteStep RPC path (execute_step_inner) applies no plan-mode, leaf or rung refusal. Those checks live only in the agent loop. A caller of ExecuteStep can therefore run workspace_edit outside those checks, the same existing gap as save_memory. The switch, ZDR refusal and capability gate still apply.

No test drives a workspace_edit or workspace_put through execute_step_inner under WORKSPACE_TOOLS=read, or under zdr or waived, and asserts the refusal before the capability gate. Only admits() is unit-tested.
The exclusive lock covers only each call's own execution. A background process started by process_start keeps writing the Space tree afterwards and can overwrite an edit without the model being told.

Once the switch is all but before the shared allowlist edit lands, capability-core rejects the write attestation with 403. Check whether a rejected id in the heartbeat batch also blocks the cap.workspace.read attestation, which would make the reads unavailable too.

Migration 0019 fills a gap below the already-present 0020-0025. That is safe only because docker-entrypoint.sh re-applies every *.up.sql idempotently on each boot. A version-tracking migrator would skip it.
execute_process_tool holds the run's workspace lock exclusively for every process tool, including read, list and signal. Narrowing it to start and stdin would keep reads concurrent.

state.rs take_hydrated_workspace removes the run's lock entry, so a workspace or process call that starts after the terminal release gets a fresh lock and loses exclusion. Confirm that no such call can run after release.
